doc.name: A — knives catalogue, night street, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: damascus chef knife
Category: knives
Shot programme: night street
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium knives product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the back-label view in a night street treatment.

SUBJECT. A damascus chef knife. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Rotated to show the reverse face, ingredient panel or hardware detail. Shoot on a 24-70mm zoom at the long end at f/2, framing for a shallow out-of-focus foreground element occluding the lower third.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard side light with 80 percent of the frame falling into shadow. Stage the product on or against mirrored steel, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a cinematic grade with a warm key and green-leaning ambient shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
